# Skills reference

Generated from `skills/*/SKILL.md` frontmatter. Each skill works on its own (`npx skills add furkansarikaya/proofline --skill <name>`).

| Skill | Description | Version |
|---|---|---|
| `api-design` | Designs or changes API contracts. Uses the project's existing contract format when one exists (OpenAPI/Swagger, GraphQL SDL, protobuf, JSON Schema) and edits that; writes docs/design/API.md only when no contract exists. Covers endpoints (METHOD /path), request/response shapes, errors, auth, idempotency, pagination and versioning, and flags every breaking and every versioned-contract change so the lead can name it in PLAN "## Contracts". Also reverse-engineers the contract documentation from existing code on "/proofline design api". Use when a task adds or changes an API surface. | 0.0.1 |
| `data-design` | Designs the data side of a change for the project's actual database - data model, Mermaid ERD, invariants, and a migration plan with expand/contract steps, batched idempotent resumable backfill, reversibility and rollback per step, lock risk per statement, and a data-loss assessment. Classifies every planned or implemented statement mechanically (scripts/classify-migration.mjs); a destructive migration makes the task CRITICAL and stops for user approval. Also reverse-engineers docs/design/DATA_MODEL.md from an existing schema, and, as the REVIEW_DATA focus, checks implemented migrations against the frozen PLAN "## Data". Use when persistence or schema changes, on "/proofline design data", or for a data review gate. | 0.0.1 |
| `debug-proof` | Debugs a failure with proof instead of guesses. Reproduces the bug with a failing command or test, lists ranked falsifiable hypotheses, narrows with logging, input bisection and `git bisect run` (in a worktree) when a known-good commit exists, proves the root cause with an experiment that flips the failure by changing only the cause, applies the minimal fix, and adds a regression test that fails before and passes after. Keeps a ledger of every experiment and outcome. Covers build-error resolution. Never reports "fixed" without the regression test. Use for bugs, failing tests, crashes and build or compile errors, or on "/proofline debug". | 0.0.1 |
| `design-sync` | Checks durable design documents against the code and reports drift as `doc:line -> missing code fact` - every table in DATA_MODEL.md exists in the schema or migrations, every path in ARCHITECTURE.md exists, every endpoint in API.md (or an OpenAPI file) exists in the routes, every token and component named in DESIGN.md exists where the doc says. Also reverse-engineers those documents from existing code (system, data, api, ui). Use in the verify gate, standalone with --check, or as a first step in a project that has code but no design docs. Heuristic misses are reported as unverifiable, never as drift. | 0.0.1 |
| `evidence-map` | Bounded codebase investigation that returns compact, verified evidence. Takes one assignment (objective, allowed scope, expected output, stop condition) and maps the live implementation, its callers, tests, patterns to follow, dependencies, constraints, affected files, regression risk and conflicting or dead duplicate implementations. Every claim is a `path:symbol` or `path:line` checked by reading or grepping; unverifiable statements are dropped or listed as open questions. A bundled script mechanically re-verifies every claim before the result is returned. Also defines how the lead consolidates several Explorer results into EVIDENCE.md. `impact` mode: a JSON report of what changed symbols reach (references, modules, contracts, tests) with stated limits. Use before planning a change in unfamiliar code, or when the proofline lead dispatches an Explorer. | 0.0.1 |
| `exploit-proof` | Defensive security review of a change in the user's own repository (working tree, branch or pull request) before merge. Enumerates the entry points the diff touches, follows untrusted data to sensitive sinks (SQL and query builders, shell, filesystem paths, HTML output, outbound URL fetches, deserializers, authorization decisions, secrets and crypto), tries to refute every candidate, and reports only confirmed vulnerabilities - traced (concrete input, file:line per hop, why each guard fails) or reproduced (a regression test in the project's own test framework, run in a throwaway git worktree). Everything else is a suspicion. Used by the Security Reviewer for the SECURITY gate (any finding -> FAIL, never waivable) or standalone on request. | 0.0.1 |
| `intent-grill` | Interviews the user about a vague or high-stakes request before a task is written. Builds a tree of the open decisions (scope, behavior, data, UI, failure modes, non-goals), asks one question at a time in dependency order with options, a recommended answer and why, never answers on the user's behalf, and stops when every branch is resolved or explicitly deferred by the user. Writes INTENT.md (decisions with who decided each, deferred items, acceptance-criteria and out-of-scope candidates) that feeds task-author and plan-contract. Use for COMPLEX or CRITICAL requests, when a request leaves behavior open, or when the user asks to be grilled ("/proofline task --grill"). | 0.0.1 |
| `plan-contract` | "Writes an executable, scoped PLAN.md for one task and validates it mechanically. YAML `scope:` front matter lists every file the change may touch, each mapped to at least one acceptance criterion; every criterion maps back to a scope path or an explicit test. Adds only the sections the task's class and scope require (Architecture for COMPLEX/CRITICAL, Data with `destructive: yes\|no` when persistence changes, UI when UI changes), plus Behavior, Tests, Verification commands, and explicit Dependencies, Contracts and Assumptions (a risk register; an unverified high-risk entry stops the freeze until the user answers). TDD exemptions need a specific reason. A bundled validator checks mapping both ways, required sections, path existence, globs and duplicates. Use when the proofline lead plans a task before freeze, or standalone to turn a TASK.md into a reviewable plan." | 0.0.1 |
| `proof-review` | Reviews a code change (uncommitted work, a branch, or a PR) and reports only what it can prove. First checks whether the change does what it says, using claims taken from the user, the PR description, linked issues, and commit messages, never inferred from the code. Then checks the change against the team's written project rules (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, Cursor and Copilot rules, CONTRIBUTING.md, ADRs), reporting only checkable rules the diff newly breaks. Then hunts bugs in the changed code and its direct callers, reporting a bug only when a temporary test reproduced it in a separate git worktree or a concrete input was traced line by line. Style, naming, suggestions, and severity scores are out of scope. Never fixes code. Inside a proofline run the intent source is the frozen PLAN.md (each acceptance criterion is a claim, any changed path outside its scope is unrequested), a focus parameter (plan, rules, bugs, rules+tests, all) selects what is reviewed, and the gate result is computed by a rule. Use when the user asks to review a change, PR, branch, or uncommitted work with proof, or when the proofline lead dispatches a review focus. | 0.0.1 |
| `proofline-lead` | The proofline lead's lifecycle method for the main session (AGENT_ROLE unset = lead). Takes a request or task through intake, classification, branch and baseline, discovery, design, plan, freeze, one implementer, tiered independent gates, the bounded fix loop, completion report and cleanup, with `agent.sh next` as the single source of the next step. Dispatches each specialist on its configured runtime (Claude Agent tool or dispatch.sh), relays specialist questions verbatim, never writes product code, never records or waives a verdict, and stops for plan approval (supervised), destructive operations, scope changes, commit, push and PR. Consumes only result headers and tables. Serves /proofline, run, resume, queue, task, design, review, audit, debug, deliver and clean. Use as the main session in a project where proofline is installed. | 0.0.1 |
| `proofline` | "The user-facing /proofline entry point. `$ARGUMENTS` is the subcommand: init, upgrade, doctor, status (default), queue, clean and version run through the proofline CLI (`bin/proofline`); run, resume, task, design, review, audit, debug and deliver hand the session to the proofline-lead skill, which carries each out through `agent.sh` and the specialist roles. Use to install proofline in a project, check that its rules are enforced, or start, resume and deliver a task." | 0.0.1 |
| `qa-plan` | Independent QA in two phases. Before implementation, writes QA_PLAN.md from the task's acceptance criteria - one concrete acceptance scenario per criterion plus adversarial scenarios only for categories that apply, each with how it will be executed. After implementation, executes the frozen plan against the real code and writes QA_REPORT.md with a mechanical PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED verdict; the plan is never weakened after seeing the code. Use for STANDARD and larger tasks, or to QA any change against its stated criteria. | 0.0.1 |
| `system-design` | Designs the smallest valid architecture for a task, or reverse-engineers docs/design/ARCHITECTURE.md from an existing codebase. C4-style levels (context, container, component) only as deep as the change needs, every component mapped to a verified repo path, boundaries, compatibility, migration concerns, trade-offs, and numbered ADRs only for decisions with real alternatives. Writes the PLAN "## Architecture" text and design/ARCHITECTURE.md inside a run. Use for COMPLEX/CRITICAL tasks, when a change crosses component boundaries, or on "/proofline design system". Never designs speculative structure. | 0.0.1 |
| `task-author` | Turns a one-sentence request or an external issue (GitHub, Jira, Linear, markdown) into the canonical TASK.md - goal, context, numbered observable acceptance criteria, explicit out of scope, constraints, risks, suggested class with the indicator that placed it - and renders it into a per-target template (project templates in .agents/templates/tasks/ win over the bundled ones). Use before planning or implementing any non-trivial change, to import a ticket, or to export a task to an issue tracker. Asks the user once when something is ambiguous; never invents requirements. | 0.0.1 |
| `tdd-proof` | Implements a change test-first with recorded proof. For every non-exempt scope path it records RED (the new behaviour's assertion fails, for the right reason), GREEN (the same test passes and nothing else broke) and optional REFACTOR through `agent.sh worker-evidence` in a run, or a local ledger standalone. A compile, type, import, syntax or setup error, a missing file or a runner finding no tests is NOT RED; a minimal stub makes the test compile first. Before GREEN is accepted the production change is reverted or mutated in a separate worktree and the new test must fail again (hollow-test check). Use whenever code is implemented or fixed. | 0.0.1 |
| `test-trust` | Audits how far a test suite can be trusted, using runnable evidence instead of opinion. Finds flaky tests (nondeterministic or order-dependent), hollow tests (stay green when the code they protect is broken, proven by targeted mutation), and slow tests (relative to the scope's own median). Two modes - full audits an explicit scope, diff is the proofline review gate's tests focus (changed tests and tests covering changed units, with a computed PASS or FAIL). Language- and framework-agnostic; discovers how the project runs its tests and proves runner capabilities before relying on them. Reports findings only, never fixes. Use when the user asks "can I trust these tests?", wants a flaky, hollow, or slow test audit of a specific scope, or when the proofline lead dispatches the tests focus of a review. | 0.0.1 |
| `ui-design` | Designs UI work. Reverse-engineers a DESIGN.md design system (tokens, typography, spacing, colour roles, components, accessibility baseline) from the existing UI when it is absent, and writes the per-task UI spec (screens, flows, every state including empty, loading, error, success, partial and permission-denied, copy, keyboard and screen-reader behaviour, responsive rules) that goes into PLAN "## UI" and design/UI.md. Reuses existing tokens and components, verified by path, before inventing new ones. Use when a task changes UI, or on "/proofline design ui". | 0.0.1 |
| `verify-proof` | Mechanical proof that a frozen plan was implemented - every acceptance criterion has a passing test or, when every mapped PLAN scope path has a tdd_exemption, recorded passing command evidence; changed paths stay inside scope; build, test and lint commands pass. Writes VERIFY.md ending in one Verdict line. | 0.0.1 |
